claim: A taxpayer dissatisfied with the valuation or equalization of real property may apply to appeal to the county board of equalization.

The application is due on or before the later of September 15 of the current year or the last day of a 45-day period beginning on the day the county auditor provides the valuation notice (59-2-919.1).
The county board of equalization must decide each appeal within 60 days after the application is made (the Tax Commission may approve an extension).
A taxpayer dissatisfied with the county board's decision may appeal to the State Tax Commission under 59-2-1006.
Tangible taxable property is assessed and taxed at a uniform and equal rate on the basis of fair market value as valued on January 1 (no separate assessment ratio is stated in this subsection).

Residential property is allowed a residential exemption equal to a 45% reduction in fair market value for a calendar year (subject to other provisions).
The residential exemption is limited to one primary residence per household (with exceptions in 59-2-103(6)(b)).
Utah Exemptions Act homestead (creditor protection): up to $42,000 in value if the property is the individual's primary personal residence; $5,000 otherwise.
For jointly owned primary residences each owner is entitled to an exemption, with a maximum of $84,000 per household.

Most Utah foreclosures are nonjudicial ('trustee sales') done without a court case.
Trustee may not exercise power of sale until a notice of default is recorded and at least three months have elapsed; notice of sale is then given.
Notice of trustee's sale must be posted at least 20 days before sale on the property and at the county recorder's office.
Notice of sale is published once a week for three weeks and a copy is mailed at least 20 days before sale.
Within three months of recording the notice of default, the trustor or successor may cure by paying the amount due (excluding accelerated principal) plus costs and fees, reinstating the obligation.
Within three months after a trustee sale, an action may be brought for the deficiency; judgment may not exceed indebtedness plus costs minus fair market value at sale date.

Real property sold on execution: officer posts notice on the property, at place of sale, at district courthouse and at three other public places for at least 21 days, and publishes weekly for three successive weeks.
Sales are at auction to the highest bidder, Monday through Saturday (legal holidays excluded), 9:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.; real property is sold at the district courthouse of the county.
Real property sold may be redeemed within 180 days after the sale by the defendant or a junior lienholder (or successors).

A personal representative may sell, mortgage, or lease any real or personal property of the estate.
A small estate affidavit cannot be used to transfer title to real property such as land or a house; probate may be needed.
